id.description: Stable row identifier. Never reuse an id for different behaviour.

axes.description: The cell this row claims in its block's coverage product. Read by the ledger.

dimensions.description: Pinned context that is NOT an axis of this block. Documentation, not coverage.

provenance.description: Why this row exists: a ticket id, a commit sha, 'coverage-gap', 'characterization', or 'discover@<sha>'.

characterization.description: Records current behaviour rather than asserting intended behaviour. Must be stated, never implied.

calendar_sensitive.description: Expectation depends on the absolute calendar (leap day, month length, yday==1, DST). Live runner cannot shift it.

needs_forward_time.description: Needs the clock to move forward (trial end, deferred downgrade). Live runner cannot drive it.

custom_spec.description: Escape hatch: path to a hand-written spec that replaces the interpreted timeline.

math.description: How the expected numbers are derived. Mandatory whenever a non-zero amount is expected; a math line that does not derive its expect is a lint failure.

at.description: ISO8601 instant to materialise setup at, for rows whose whole action IS the setup (a resource-characterization row). Mutually exclusive with `timeline`.

no_transaction.description: Run this row with DatabaseCleaner's deletion strategy instead of a wrapping transaction (RSpec `transaction: false`). Required by anything using idempotent_transaction — notably progressive billing — which refuses to run inside an open transaction.

pins.description: Finding ids this row holds still (see scratchpad FINDINGS.md, e.g. F01). A row that pins a finding is what stops that bug moving unnoticed; the ledger reports findings with no pinning row.

custom_aggregation.description: Org flag gating custom_agg metrics (BillableMetrics::CreateService:20). Not the premium licence — a separate switch.

custom_aggregator.description: Ruby source defining aggregate(event, previous_state, aggregation_properties); required for custom_agg.

interval.description: null is meaningful: a blank interval is a B14 rejection row, so it must survive into the payload rather than being defaulted.

invoice_grace_period.description: Sent under billing_configuration by the runner; a top-level value is dropped by strong params.

activation_rules.description: Gates activation until the rule is satisfied. Applied only at creation, while the subscription is still `pending` (Subscriptions::ActivationRules::ApplyService refuses any other status). A `payment` rule is applicable only on a pay_in_advance plan outside a trial (subscription/activation_rule/payment.rb:5-7); otherwise it resolves not_applicable and the subscription activates normally.

timeout_hours.description: Hours before a pending rule expires. 0 (the column default) means never.

plan_overrides.description: Creates an override plan. fixed_charges entries may name add_on_code/code instead of the UUID the API wants; the runner resolves it.

coupons.description: Coupons created and applied to the customer. `expiration` is mandatory — omitting it fails with expiration/value_is_invalid.

applies_to.description: Limitations. Absent means the wallet pays for anything.

recurring_transaction_rules.description: Automatic top-ups. `trigger: interval` re-arms on a schedule, `trigger: threshold` when the balance falls below threshold_credits; `method: target` tops up TO target_ongoing_balance rather than BY a fixed amount.

add_ons.description: One-off priced items. A fixed charge prices an add-on on a plan, so add-ons are also the prerequisite for setup.fixed_charges.

fixed_charges.description: Recurring priced units on the plan, independent of metered usage. Created AFTER the plan: inlining them in POST /plans returns 500, so the runner posts them to /plans/:code/fixed_charges.

add_on_code.description: must name an add-on the row declares

plans.description: ADDITIONAL plans beyond setup.plan, so a row can move a subscription between them (upgrade/downgrade). Each carries its own charges; setup.charges belongs to setup.plan. A timeline step selects one with params.plan_code.

at.description: ISO8601 instant. travel_to for rspec; shifted for live.

precise_total_amount_cents.description: Top-level event field, not a property. The dynamic charge model takes its amount from here.

params.description: Free-form body for the mutation verbs. On update_plan, a `charges` entry may name `billable_metric_code` instead of the `billable_metric_id` UUID the endpoint requires (plans_controller.rb:122-131) — the runner resolves it against the metric the setup created. An entry carrying no `id` therefore REPLACES the charge for that metric: Plans::UpdateService creates it (update_service.rb:230-235) and sanitize_charges discards the one the array omitted (:241-248), which is the only way a row can rewrite a charge_id without cloning a plan.

invoice_type.description: pay_invoice: which invoice to settle, by type. Defaults to the most recent.

credit_note.description: create_credit_note: items are PRE-TAX per fee; credit/refund/offset amounts are the tax-INCLUSIVE totals.

invoice_type.description: which invoice to credit; defaults to the most recent

charge.description: update_plan_charge: the charge to update on the PARENT plan. Charge codes default to the metric code, so the metric code identifies it.

cascade_updates.description: propagate the change to child (overridden) plans

filters.description: The charge's filter set, as a REPLACEMENT array — one verb for create, update and delete. Entries are resolved against the filters already on the charge by their `values` (ChargeFilters::CreateOrUpdateBatchService), never by id, because a row cannot know a filter's UUID: a new `values` combination creates, a known one with new `properties` updates, and an omitted one is discarded. `filters: []` deletes them all.

charge_model.description: Mandatory: PUT /plans/:code/charges/:code is a full replacement, so omitting it fails with charge_model/value_is_mandatory.

one_off.description: create_one_off_invoice: POST /api/v1/invoices, the only route that can produce a fee with `fee_type: :add_on` (assigned in exactly one place app-wide, fees/one_off_service.rb:40, reached only from Invoices::CreateOneOffService). The invoice it makes is `invoice_type: one_off` and always finalized — only Invoices::SubscriptionService consults the grace period (subscription_service.rb:193) — so it has no draft, and Invoices::RefreshDraftService refuses it outright with `return result.forbidden_failure! unless invoice.subscription?` (refresh_draft_service.rb:32). It is also absent from #preview_params (invoices_controller.rb:336-381), which permits no `fees` key at all. An add-on fee is therefore observable on a finalized invoice and nowhere else.

add_ons.description: Codes of add-ons the row declared in setup.add_ons, one fee each. Named by code because `fees[].add_on_code` is the only identifier InvoicesController#create_params permits (invoices_controller.rb:296-303).

units.description: Units for EVERY fee in the call, not per add-on: ScenariosHelper#create_one_off_invoice takes one `units:` for the whole list. Two add-ons that must differ therefore differ by their own setup.add_ons `amount_cents`, which becomes each fee's `unit_amount_cents`. Defaults to 1.

tax_codes.description: Explicit tax codes on EVERY fee in the call — the first rung of the Fees::ApplyTaxesService ladder (`return ...taxes.where(code: tax_codes) if tax_codes`, apply_taxes_service.rb:64-66), and POST /api/v1/invoices is the only route that carries them. An empty array is NOT a distinct assertion here: Fees::OneOffService gates on `tax_codes.present?` (one_off_service.rb:56), so `[]` never reaches ApplyTaxesService and behaves exactly like omitting the key — the ladder falls through to the add-on rung either way. Say the codes or say nothing.

fixed_charge.description: update_plan_fixed_charge / update_subscription_fixed_charge: which fixed charge to move, and to how many units. Both endpoints are addressed by the charge's CODE, which the runner defaults to the add-on's code on creation, so a row names `add_on_code` and needs no UUID. update_plan_fixed_charge moves the PLAN's units (and so every subscription on it that has no override of its own); update_subscription_fixed_charge moves ONE subscription's, writing a Subscription::FixedChargeUnitsOverride that a later plan-level update then skips. The subscription endpoint is premium-only, so rows using it need `premium: true`.

add_on_code.description: the fixed charge's code, which defaults to the add-on's code

code.description: the fixed charge's code, when the row gave it one that is not the add-on's

units.description: Mandatory. FixedCharges::UpdateService assigns `units` unconditionally, so an omitted value nulls the column rather than leaving it alone; and the new FixedChargeEvent is only emitted when the units actually moved (update_service.rb:35, :44).

apply_units_immediately.description: WHEN the new units take effect, and the whole point of the B13 units_change axis. FixedCharges::EmitEventsService stamps the new FixedChargeEvent at Time.current when true and at fixed_charges_period_to_datetime + 1.second when false (emit_events_service.rb:22) — the second is outside the current period's range, so the period bills the OLD units and the change shows up next period. Forwarded on presence of the KEY, not truthiness: `false` is the deferred half of the axis, not an omission.

properties.description: Mandatory for update_plan_fixed_charge: the endpoint replaces properties, and omitting them falls back to ChargeModels::BuildDefaultPropertiesService — amount "0" for a standard charge (update_service.rb:36-38) — so a units-only row would silently reprice the charge to nothing. Optional on the subscription endpoint, where sending it switches the service off the units-only override path onto the plan-clone path (fixed_charge_units_override_detection_concern.rb:26-31).

charge_model.description: Mandatory for update_plan_fixed_charge — it selects the fallback properties above. It does NOT change the charge model once the plan has subscriptions: `fixed_charge.charge_model = params[:charge_model] unless plan.attached_to_subscriptions?` (update_service.rb:31), so resend the existing one.

code.description: which resource the mutation targets (update_tax, update_coupon, delete_metric, top_up_wallet); defaults to the first the setup declared. On top_up_wallet it is what makes two wallets distinguishable at all — the lookup is otherwise unordered, so a two-wallet row without it funds one at random.

select.description: which invoice the step acts on; same shape as an expectation's select. Defaults to the newest.

stage.description: Which call must be rejected. Every stage but `usage` is a setup call; `usage` is the GET current_usage a fetch_current_usage step performs, asserted at that step, which is how a refusal-only cell (current-usage after termination, 405 no_active_subscription) is expressible at all. Deliberately limited to what the interpreter implements (GoldenRunner::SUPPORTED_ERROR_STAGES) — harness_spec.rb asserts the two agree, because a stage the schema permits but the runner ignores lets a row assert nothing and pass. Named `stage`, not `on`: YAML 1.1 reads a bare `on` key as boolean true.

invoices.description: Total invoice count for the customer.

invoice.description: One invoice expectation, or a list of them when the row asserts money moving between invoices. Each entry in a list must carry its own `select`.

wallet.description: A single wallet, or a list. The multi-wallet-priority axis is defined by what the OTHER wallet kept, so a two-wallet row asserts both balances rather than inferring the second arithmetically.

preview.description: The un-persisted invoice returned by POST /invoices/preview. Same assertable fields as a real invoice, which is the point: a preview that disagrees with the invoice it predicts is the bug.

invoice_expectation.description: Assertable-field allowlist. Volatile fields (lago_id, number, sequential_id, created_at, issuing_date, file_url) are deliberately absent so no row can pin them.

units.description: Compared as BigDecimal (GoldenComparison::NUMERIC_FIELDS), so 20 and "20.0" are the same assertion. Both spellings are permitted because the schema said `string` only while two green B9 rows had always written the integer — a rule the comparator never enforced and nothing but the integrity example could see.

from_date.description: V1::FeeSerializer names the period boundaries from_date/to_date, not from_datetime.

resource_expectation.description: Assert attributes of a resource the setup created. For characterization rows where the API accepts the request but normalises the input, so there is no error to assert.

code.description: which one, when the row declares several; defaults to the first

credit_note_expectation.description: Assertable fields of the created credit note. Volatile fields (lago_id, number, sequential_id, created_at) are deliberately absent.

select.description: Which credit note. Absent means the one created by this row's create_credit_note step; present reads the customer's credit notes, which is the only way to assert one Lago created by itself.

index.description: into the matched notes, oldest first; -1 is the newest

wallet_expectation.description: State of a wallet after the timeline. The only way to assert WHICH wallet paid, or what a balance became — an invoice alone cannot show either.

code.description: which wallet, when the row declares several; defaults to the first

lifetime_usage_expectation.description: Cumulative usage across the subscription's whole life, which is what progressive-billing thresholds are measured against — deliberately not per-period like current usage.

select.description: Scopes the read to one subscription STATUS. subscriptions/base_controller.rb:20 resolves external_id together with `status: params[:status] || :active`, so without this the read 404s the moment the subscription stops being active — which is the whole of B7's lifetime-usage after-termination column. A `select` on its own is refused by the interpreter: it satisfies minProperties while asserting nothing.
